subject: Acme POC: evaluation plan & rubric — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: James Liu <james.liu@acmecorp.com>, Elena Gomez <egomez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC: evaluation plan & rubric — next steps

Hi James / Elena —

Great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking us through the scoring priorities and the three primary evaluation intents: 1) accuracy on domain Q&A, 2) hallucination rate on constrained documents, and 3) latency under 300ms for single-query lookups.

As discussed, attached is a draft POC evaluation plan and an initial grading rubric (attached). High-level items we agreed to capture:
- Success criteria (pass/fail thresholds) for each intent
- Offline eval set (sample prompts & reference answers) vs online shadowing methodology
- Ownership & timeline for data collection and annotation
- Success measurement & rollout decision gate (metrics + stakeholders)

Quick ask / next steps:
1) Please confirm the three success criteria below by EOD Friday so we can finalize the POC timeline.
   - Accuracy: >= 88% on Acme domain Q&A sample set (measured offline, top-1 exact/semantic match)
   - Hallucination: < 5% on constrained-doc retrieval tests (measured via manual annotation on 200 samples)
   - Latency: p95 < 300ms for single-turn retrieval+answer on your representative queries (online shadow test)
2) We included a recommended split: first two weeks offline evals + rubric tuning, then 2 weeks online shadowing in production-like environment. Is that alignment okay?

I've attached: Acme_POC_eval_plan_v1.pdf and eval_grading_rubric_v2.xlsx. I also uploaded a sample prompt set to the linked doc.

If that looks good I'll schedule a quick 30-min sync Monday to lock owners and finalize the instrumentation checklist (logging, trace ids, ground-truth capture).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Acme_POC_eval_plan_v1.pdf (POC plan), eval_grading_rubric_v2.xlsx (rubric), sample_prompt_set.csv (30 sample prompts)

From: James Liu <james.liu@acmecorp.com>

Date: 2026-03-16 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC: evaluation plan & rubric — next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and for putting this together. High level thumbs up on the approach. A few clarifying notes from our side before we commit:

- Accuracy target: 88% sounds reasonable but we need to ensure the reference answers reflect the nuance in our support docs. Our SME team (Elena cc'd) can provide a 500-sample set and highlight ambiguous items.
- Hallucination: the <5% sounds strict but acceptable if we limit the retrieval scope properly. Can you confirm how Redwood will define a hallucination in the rubric (e.g., fabricated facts vs. unsupported inference)?
- Latency: p95 <300ms is our target for latency-sensitive flows; we can accept p50/p95 split too if you recommend (e.g., p50 <150ms, p95 <300ms).

Regarding timeline, a 4-week window (2 offline + 2 shadow) is workable. Procurement will need a short SOW; procurement@acmecorp.com is cc'd on this thread — they will handle contracting.

Can you send a version of the rubric with explicit definitions and a short example for each rubric category? That will speed our SME annotation.

—James
Head of AI Integrations, Acme Corp

On an unrelated note: we may want to shadow only a sampled 10% of live traffic to start so we don't impact their current logging pipeline.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: James Liu <james.liu@acmecorp.com>, Elena Gomez <egomez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-17 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC: evaluation plan & rubric — next steps

James / Elena —

Great feedback — thanks. Quick replies inline below and attached an updated rubric with explicit definitions and two examples per category (eval_grading_rubric_v2.xlsx -> v2.1 in the doc link).

- Hallucination definition: we define a hallucination as any model output that asserts a verifiable fact that is not supported by the retrieved context or the provided knowledge base. The rubric has three levels: Correct (answer consistent with KB), Incomplete (partial answer / missing citation), Hallucination (fabricated or contradicted). We included examples for each.
- Latency targets: we recommend tracking both p50 and p95. We'll instrument p50 <150ms and p95 <300ms as the POC gates.
- Offline vs online:
   * Week 1-2: Offline eval — Redwood provides a sanitized eval harness and runs the candidate model(s) against your SME-labeled reference set. We will return per-prompt metrics, confusion analysis, and example failures for annotation review.
   * Week 3-4: Online shadow — we run a shadow variant on a sampled fraction of live queries (default 10%) and capture model output + context. Your SMEs will annotate a stratified sample (200-400 items) for hallucination and correctness to validate offline signals.

Ownership suggestions:
- Acme SME lead: Elena (annotations + reference answer sign-off)
- Redwood: Marissa (POC technical lead), Vivek (inference config & deployment)
- Acme infra/production: James (shadow rollout & logging access)

Action items I will take this week:
- Finalize the eval harness config and provide the script for running offline evals
- Share an instrumentation checklist for shadowing (logging keys, user-id hashing, retention notes)

Can we lock a 30-minute sync Monday 3/22 10am PT to finalize owners and procurement needs? If that works I will send a calendar invite and attach the SOW stub for procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Acme POC: evaluation plan & rubric — next steps

Hey team —

I'm the product lead helping with eval methodology. I reviewed the rubric and added two recommended columns in the spreadsheet: (1) "Annotation effort" (est. minutes per item) and (2) "Reliability check" (we recommend double annotation on 10% sample to estimate inter-annotator agreement). These will help quantify annotation cost and set confidence intervals on the offline metrics.

A couple tactical suggestions:
- For offline accuracy, use both exact match and a relaxed semantic-similarity threshold (0.7 cosine on embeddings) to account for paraphrases. We'll provide per-prompt examples where exact-match fails but semantic-match succeeds.
- For hallucination sampling in shadow, stratify by low-retrieval-confidence queries (where retriever score < threshold) because those are higher-risk for fabrication.

I've updated eval_grading_rubric_v2.xlsx with the additions and a short section on suggested annotation tooling (Doccano / Label Studio). Attaching the file here for convenience.

Rachel Kim
Product Manager, Evals
Redwood Inference
